attribution.note: Marcus makes this prediction in his own prose.

semantics.note: The normalization captures litigation and disclosures but omits the prediction that investors will feel wronged and broadens the reference beyond those losing money during the preceding weeks.

contract.note: The contract reasonably reads the statement as predicting litigation, expressed grievances and substantial disclosures caused by litigation. It preserves the absence of a deadline.

evidence.note: The dated complaint establishes preexisting shareholder litigation. It does not establish post-statement litigation or substantial new information made public through litigation.

reviews.rationale: The packet establishes an existing complaint but no substantial disclosures caused by the relevant litigation. The early-resolution rule is unmet. With no deadline or decisive event preventing fulfillment, neither support nor contradiction is established.
